items.question: A society has 6 members. In how many more ways can a president, a secretary and a treasurer (three different posts, one person each) be appointed than a 3-member committee with no posts be selected?
items.explanation: Posts are different, so order matters: 6P3 = 120. A committee has no order: 6C3 = 20. Difference = 120 − 20 = 100.

why_not.B: Gave only the ways to appoint office bearers, 6P3, and did not subtract the committee ways.
why_not.A: Gave only the committee ways, 6C3, and ignored the difference asked.
why_not.D: Added 120 and 20 instead of finding the difference.

items.exam_tip: Different posts mean swapping people gives a new result, so use nPr. Plain selection means nCr.

items.question: Under SA 200, an auditor plans and performs the audit with an attitude that includes a questioning mind and a critical assessment of audit evidence. What is this attitude called?
items.explanation: SA 200 defines professional skepticism as an attitude with a questioning mind, alertness to conditions indicating possible misstatement, and critical assessment of audit evidence.

why_not.A: Judgment is applying knowledge and experience to decisions, not the questioning attitude.
why_not.B: Reasonable assurance is a high level of assurance, not an attitude.
why_not.C: Materiality is a threshold for misstatements, not an attitude.

items.exam_tip: Skepticism = attitude (questioning mind). Judgment = application of knowledge and experience.
check_notes: Checker: Pure recall: the stem closely paraphrases the SA 200 definition. That is acceptable at this level, but it makes the question easy.
Checker: The stem leaves out one part of the definition, "being alert to conditions which may indicate possible misstatement due to error or fraud". This does not make the answer ambiguous.

items.paper_name: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
items.question: Under SA 505, management refuses to allow the auditor to send a confirmation request to a particular debtor. What should the auditor do first?
options: Inquire why management refuses and evaluate the reasons given
Drop the balance from testing as it is not material
Treat the refusal as proof of fraud and resign immediately
Accept the refusal and report a qualified opinion at once
items.explanation: SA 505 requires the auditor to inquire into management's reasons and seek audit evidence on their validity and reasonableness. The auditor then evaluates the effect on risk assessment and designs alternative procedures.

why_not.D: Modifying the opinion comes only after inquiry and alternative procedures fail to give evidence.
why_not.C: Refusal does not automatically prove fraud; resignation is not the first step.
why_not.B: Materiality is not assumed; the balance cannot be dropped just because management objects.

items.exam_tip: Refusal to allow confirmation: inquire, evaluate, then alternative procedures. Modify opinion only if evidence is still lacking.
check_notes: Checker: The distractors are too easy to rule out: they use extreme wording ('resign immediately', 'at once', 'proof of fraud') and an unsupported materiality assumption. Any student can eliminate them without really knowing paragraph 8 of SA 505. Better distractors would be plausible steps from later in the sequence, such as going straight to alternative procedures or straight to telling those charged with governance.

Checker: Option A leaves out part of the first step. SA 505 also requires the auditor to seek evidence on whether management's reasons are valid and reasonable, not just to evaluate them. This is a polish point only.
